name: LT4321IUF#PBF
title: LT4321: PoE ideal diode bridge controller, two channels, 100 V, 16-lead 4 mm × 4 mm QFN
summary: The LT4321 drives eight external N-channel MOSFETs as two full-wave rectifier bridges, so a Power over Ethernet powered device accepts either supply polarity on its data pairs, its spare pairs or both, without the forward drop of two diodes. A charge pump lifts the top gates above the output, so every bridge switch is an NMOS. The sense inputs are high impedance, a pair's MOSFETs turn on only when one input of that pair is above OUTP and the other below OUTN, and with OUTP below 10 V the part draws 0.8 µA typical, 5 µA maximum, so it stays out of the way of PD detection. LT4321IUF#PBF is the -40 °C to 85 °C grade; the H grade runs to 125 °C.

circuits.title: Powered Device for PoE (to 13W), PoE+ (to 25.5W), or Linear LTPoE++ (to 90W) Systems
circuits.description: A powered device taking power from both the data pairs (RJ-45 1/2 and 3/6) and the spare pairs (4/5 and 7/8). The four transformer centre taps feed IN12, IN36, IN45 and IN78 and the eight MOSFETs Q1-Q8 form two bridges onto OUTP/OUTN. C1 (0.1 µF) and the SMAJ60A TVS sit across OUTP and OUTN. /EN is tied to OUTP so EN alone enables the bridge; the LT4275 PD controller's PWRGD drives EN and the isolated supply's RUN, so the bridge comes on after detection and classification. The LT4275 switches the 10 µF capacitor and the supply onto the port through the hot-swap FET Q9.

parts.note: four centre-tapped windings on the cable side, one per RJ-45 pair

circuits.title: Figure 3. PD Interface Using the EN Pin
circuits.description: The active-high EN input follows the LT4275's PWRGD output, with a 100 kΩ pull-up R1 to OUTP; /EN is tied to OUTP so it never holds the part on. The same PWRGD line runs the isolated supply. C1 and the TVS bypass OUTP to OUTN; the 10 µF capacitor sits behind the hot-swap FET Q1.
notes: The bridge MOSFETs and the LT4321 inputs connect as in the typical application.

circuits.title: Figure 4. PD Interface Using the /EN Pin
circuits.description: The PD controller is an LTC4265, which switches the negative return: its GND pin is on OUTP, VIN on OUTN, and its VOUT is the switched return RTN for the 10 µF capacitor and the isolated supply. Its active-low /PWRGD, pulled up to OUTP through R1 (100 kΩ), drives the LT4321's /EN; EN is tied to OUTN. The active-high PWRGD, pulled up by R2 (100 kΩ), runs the supply.
notes: Ground in this circuit is OUTP, the LTC4265's GND.
The bridge MOSFETs and the LT4321 inputs connect as in the typical application.

circuits.title: High Efficiency 25W PD Solution with 12VDC and 24VAC Auxiliary Input
circuits.description: A 25 W PD that runs from PoE or from an auxiliary 9 V to 57 V DC or 24 V AC input. The LT4321 with eight PSMN075-100MSE MOSFETs and a Würth 749022017 transformer rectifies the data and spare pairs onto OUTP/OUTN, bypassed by 0.1 µF and an SMAJ60A. The LT4275B switches the port through a PSMN075-100MSE hot-swap FET onto the 680 µF output rail, with 3.3 kΩ and 150 nF from HSGATE to OUTN and a 34.8 Ω class resistor; IEEEUVLO is tied to OUTN. The auxiliary input is rectified by an LT4320 ideal bridge with four BSZ110N06NS3 MOSFETs straight onto the output rail, bypassed by 1 µF. Two MMSD4148 diodes peak-detect the auxiliary input onto a 0.1 µF capacitor that feeds the LT4275B's AUX pin through a 158 kΩ / 931 kΩ divider; a third MMSD4148 joins that node to the output rail. PWRGD drives the LT4321's EN and, with a 100 kΩ pull-up to the rail, the isolated supply's RUN.

notes: Misprint: the spare-pair bridge has IN45 and IN78 swapped between its two MOSFET legs; it should read TG45 and BG45 on IN45 (pins 4/5), TG78 and BG78 on IN78 (pins 7/8).

circuits.title: LTPoE++ 70W Powered Device
circuits.description: A 70 W LTPoE++ PD on all four pairs: the LT4321 drives eight PSMN075-100MSE MOSFETs fed from a Würth 749022016 transformer, with 0.1 µF and an SMAJ60A across OUTP and OUTN. The LT4275 switches the port through a PSMN040-100MSE hot-swap FET onto a 22 µF rail; 3.3 kΩ in series with 47 nF hangs from HSGATE to OUTN, 64.9 Ω on RCLASS++ and 76.8 Ω on RCLASS set the classification, and AUX and /IEEEUVLO are tied to OUTN. PWRGD drives the LT4321's EN and the isolated supply's RUN, pulled up to the rail by 100 kΩ.

equations.name: MOSFET on-resistance for a chosen forward drop

where.RDS(ON): channel resistance of each external bridge MOSFET
where.VF: forward drop wanted across a conducting MOSFET, 20 mV to 70 mV for best savings

equations.note: Worked case: a PoE+ class 4 PD averages up to 600 mA; with VF = 40 mV, RDS(ON) = 40 mV / 600 mA = 66 mΩ, and the bridge then dissipates about one fifteenth of a B2100 Schottky diode bridge.

operation.text: Two independent DC channels, |IN12-IN36| and |IN45-IN78|, are rectified into one output. The part picks out the larger of the two and connects it to OUTP/OUTN with the right polarity. The enforced dropout ΔVSD gives a smooth handover between channels. In a PD this replaces the diode bridge that the IEEE 802.3 standard's either-polarity requirement calls for, works with straight or crossover cables and with endspan or midspan PSEs, and keeps the PD from feeding current back into the cable (Figure 1 compares dissipation with an S2B diode bridge).

operation.topic: Why not a discrete ideal bridge
operation.text: Discrete ideal bridges trade quiescent current against tolerance to transients and leakage; tuned for PoE quiescent levels, board leakage between bridge parts can turn a switch on by accident, latch the bridge up and destroy it. The LT4321 holds the MOSFETs that should be off firmly off, and its bridge tolerates hot-plugging, input shorts, common-mode shifts and board leakage.

Ideal bridge mode needs two things: OUTP above VUVLO, and one of EN or /EN asserted. It then compares each input with the outputs, pair by pair (IN12/IN36 and IN45/IN78): a pair's MOSFETs turn on only when one input of the pair is above OUTP and the other is below OUTN. With IN36 above OUTP and IN12 below OUTN, for example, TG36 and BG12 are driven on. Tables 1 and 2 list every case.

Shutdown keeps the part's quiescent current out of the way of PoE detection and classification (Figure 2). The part is always shut down while OUTP is below VUVLO, and can be held shut down over the whole operating range by deasserting both EN and /EN. Shutdown does not disconnect the load: each MOSFET's gate is shorted to its source and the eight body diodes carry the current as two ordinary diode bridges.
At light load the body-diode loss is smaller than the part's own quiescent loss, so in a low-power sleep mode the part may be shut down to save power when the load current is below 20 mA.

The high-impedance sense inputs keep reverse current out of unused pairs. When the supply dies or is shorted, the MOSFETs are switched off quickly to keep the reverse current spike short. Through transients the part does not turn on the MOSFETs of unpowered pairs.

Place a 0.1 µF ceramic across OUTP and OUTN. IEEE 802.3 limits the PD interface capacitance CPD to 0.12 µF; both chips need local bypassing and may share one 0.1 µF capacitor, or, if they cannot both sit next to it, each gets its own 0.047 µF ceramic close by. While the LT4321 is enabled at least 10 µF must also be across OUTP and OUTN: in PoE that CPORT capacitor may be switched in by the PD controller's hot-swap FET; elsewhere it may be connected permanently.

The pins are rated 100 V absolute maximum and survive brief overvoltage, but cable and remote telecom supply inputs routinely see higher peaks. Fit a unidirectional TVS such as SMAJ60A across OUTP and OUTN, as close to the LT4321 as possible. Linear Technology applications support advises on protection against extreme surge and cable-discharge levels.

The MOSFET drain-source breakdown must exceed the highest input voltage, and be at least 100 V in PoE. Gate threshold must be 2 V minimum in every application. The power saved depends on RDS(ON); choose it so the forward drop at the average load current is 20 mV to 70 mV.

Above VUVLO, EN and /EN choose between shutdown and ideal bridge mode. Either may be driven from 3.3 V or 5 V logic, or by an open drain or open collector. /EN is pulled up to the internal VENOC through 250 kΩ and EN is pulled down to OUTN through 250 kΩ; below 12 V on OUTP both pins go high impedance so these resistors do not disturb PoE detection. Both pins tolerate 100 V and may be tied straight to OUTP or OUTN. Driven from a PD interface controller's power-good output (Figures 3 and 4), the bridge comes on after detection and classification and before the PD draws much current.
